question: Why does a leaf–spine network design replace a tree-shaped network in cloud data centres?
option_a: It encrypts north–south traffic before it leaves the building

question: According to the Popek–Goldberg criterion, a machine is cleanly virtualisable only if:
option_a: every sensitive instruction is a subset of the privileged instructions, so that it traps when a demoted guest attempts it
option_b: every instruction is interpreted in software by the hypervisor
option_c: the guest operating system is modified to call the hypervisor through hypercalls
option_d: the processor has more than two privilege levels available

question: Which virtualisation approach is the cloud default, running the guest unmodified with almost all instructions executing directly on the real processor and only privileged operations trapping into the hypervisor?
Name the four pillars of the baseline that the observation commands measure, and the fifth source that complements them.
accepted_answers: cpu, memory, disk, network, plus logs; cpu, memory, disk and network; logs; cpu memory disk network logs; the four pillars are cpu, memory, disk and network, complemented by logs (journalctl)

question: In one or two sentences: what is a VM escape, and why is it the worst-case failure of isolation?
accepted_answers: code breaks out of its guest into the hypervisor, and every guest above it is exposed; an attacker escapes the virtual machine into the hypervisor and can reach the other guests; breaking out of a guest vm into the hypervisor, exposing all other tenants' guests

question: Building on the exercise "Which command for which question": during a morning check of the laboratory VM you notice that the disk is filling unusually fast and that the machine is listening on a port that was not in your recorded baseline. For each of the two observations, name the command that revealed it, state why the recorded baseline is what makes the observation meaningful, and formulate - in the vocabulary of the threat–risk–control chain - the question you would ask next for each.
sample_answer: Disk filling fast: df -h (du -sh for a directory); possible log flooding or data staged for exfiltration. Unexpected listening port: ss -tulpn; a service nobody started. The baseline matters because before something abnormal can be recognised, normal must be known - only comparison against recorded healthy values shows these as deviations. TRC question per observation: what threat could explain the deviation, how likely is it and what impact would it have, and which control would reduce that risk. Grading: two correct commands + role of the baseline + a threat–risk–control formulation for each observation.
